treemap.comment: Begin treemap at either lowercase header without imposing a suffix boundary. treemap.md#detection: Accepted headers are `treemap-beta` and `treemap`; both report diagram id `treemap`. treemap.md#headers-and-indentation: Neither header requires a word or whitespace boundary. common.md#leading-whitespace: Whitespace, line terminators, directives, and comment regions before the first unit of the diagram's lexer are trivia and are not seen by the diagram's grammar.

patterns.comment: Reuse native percent comments. treemap.md#comments-and-authored-boundaries: At a native unit start, a percent pair reads a Comment through before the next LF; in source terms CR, CRLF and LF end it after common line conversion.

Reuse title and accessibility composites without imposing a following EOL. treemap.md#common-forms: The three common terminals have the same character rules as [common.langium][common], but this diagram does not import its fragment: no EOL is required after a common form. treemap.md#common-forms: An acc-descr-block reads `accDescr`, zero or more common Notation whitespace characters, `{`, any characters up to the first `}`, and that required closer.

Read a class definition with or without style text, preserving its name and optional final semicolon. treemap.md#class-definitions: A class-definition unit consists of `classDef`, one or more common Notation whitespace characters, a class name, an optional whitespace-led style text and at most one final semicolon. treemap.md#class-definitions: Without intervening whitespace, a styleless class name may be followed immediately by a quoted row.

Read class style after its required whitespace, recognizing property names and whole values while retaining other accepted style text. treemap.md#class-definitions: The separating whitespace is read maximally before style text. It can cross line feeds and blank lines, so a following quoted row or classDef can be the style rather than a new statement. Style text itself runs through all characters before the first semicolon or line terminator, including commas, colons, quotes, percent pairs, U+2028 and U+2029. Empty style is allowed. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read an entity whole so its semicolon does not end a style. treemap.md#comments-and-authored-boundaries: Class style, common value text and string interiors are text/string positions; whitespace-only parts are transparent. common.md#entities: A directive right after the `#` or right before the `;` lies inside the entity, which is read in the text without its directives, and so do two directives right before the `;`.
patterns.name: string.unquoted.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read a styleless class definition without a value scope. treemap.md#class-definitions: Without intervening whitespace, a styleless class name may be followed immediately by a quoted row. treemap.md#class-definitions: A terminating semicolon may likewise precede the next row.

Read a selector separator and its class element name, retaining intervening directives. treemap.md#names-numbers-and-strings: An identifier starts with an ASCII letter or underscore and continues with zero or more ASCII letters, digits or underscores. treemap.md#comments-and-authored-boundaries: A directive between a common keyword and colon, or a classDef keyword and name with its required whitespace, is permitted. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

Reuse plain double-quoted row labels. treemap.md#names-numbers-and-strings: A string opens with a double or single quote and closes at the next same quote. It may be empty and may include opposite quotes, backslashes, line terminators, U+2028 and U+2029. Backslashes do not escape quotes or decode characters, and a backslash followed by a physical line feed is allowed. An unclosed string rejects. Preserve source quotes and line endings in StringLiteral.raw.

Reuse plain single-quoted row labels. treemap.md#names-numbers-and-strings: A string opens with a double or single quote and closes at the next same quote. It may be empty and may include opposite quotes, backslashes, line terminators, U+2028 and U+2029. Backslashes do not escape quotes or decode characters, and a backslash followed by a physical line feed is allowed. An unclosed string rejects. Preserve source quotes and line endings in StringLiteral.raw.

Read a numeric leaf value, keeping its commas and underscores whole after its first digit or dot. treemap.md#names-numbers-and-strings: A number unit takes as many digits, underscores, dots and commas as possible. Identifier and comma rules have priority at its start: `_12` is an identifier and `,12` starts with a comma, so neither is a leaf number. Once a digit or dot starts the number, later commas and underscores stay inside it, including trailing commas before the next quoted row.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read either leaf value separator. treemap.md#grammar: Take the leaf reading when the complete leaf production matches; otherwise a quoted name with its optional selector is a section.

treemap-style.comment: Read a style property name and its whole value; an entity remains part of the value, with no numeric subscopes. treemap.md#class-definitions: Style text itself runs through all characters before the first semicolon or line terminator, including commas, colons, quotes, percent pairs, U+2028 and U+2029. treemap.md#class-definitions: Unknown CSS, unused definitions, repeated definitions and unresolved selectors are not rejection conditions. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

treemap-style-text.comment: Read style separators and accepted opaque text that has no property colon. treemap.md#class-definitions: Unknown CSS, unused definitions, repeated definitions and unresolved selectors are not rejection conditions. treemap.md#class-definitions: Preserve each definition's whole style text; splitting and merging styles belong to the tests summary.
